transcript.text: I think my washer dryer has a fault - I put it on just a drying programme with dry-ish clothes and I can hear water running into it and draining the whole time. Surely it shouldn't use water to dry? It's a Beko.

Yes — on many Beko washer-dryers, using some cold water during a drying-only programme is normal. What would not be normal is a strong continuous fill, water overflowing, an error code, or the clothes staying cold and wet after a proper drying cycle. The useful distinction is whether it is a small intermittent trickle and the load warms/dries, versus a full-on fill with little or no drying. Is it only a small intermittent trickle of water, and does the drum/clothes become warm and gradually dry?
Yes, it's a gentle trickle with the pump coming on occasionally, and the clothes come out properly dry. The drying time counts down normally and there are no error codes.

That sounds normal rather than a fault. A washer-dryer can use a gentle flow of cold water during drying to condense the moisture removed from the clothes, and it will pump that water away periodically. Because the load warms and dries properly, the timer behaves normally and there are no error codes, there is no sign of a heating, drainage or water-inlet fault. It would only need investigating if the flow became a full fill, it started leaking, displayed an error, or drying performance worsened.
